story.fullStory:
Tony Joe White's "Polk Salad Annie" reached #8 on the Billboard Hot 100. "Polk Salad Annie" is a 1968 song written and performed by Tony Joe White.

Its lyrics describe the lifestyle of a poor rural Southern girl and her family.

Traditionally, the term to describe the type of food highlighted in the song is polk or poke salad, a dish of cooked greens made from pokeweed.

The song peaked at #8 on the Billboard Hot 100 and spent 12 weeks on the chart.

Tony Joe White (July 23, 1943 – October 24, 2018), nicknamed the Swamp Fox, was an American singer-songwriter and guitarist, best known for his 1969 hit "Polk Salad Annie" and for "Rainy Night in Georgia", which he wrote but which was first made popular by Brook Benton in 1970.
Polk Salad Annie was released in 1971.
The song appears on the album "Tony Joe White" (1971).
